items.title: Chai's FPL GW11 Bus Team! 🚌
items.headline: Haaland captained as Calafiori faces a surprise bench call for Gameweek 11
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the captain for Gameweek 11, with Manchester City hosting Fulham. He leads a front two alongside Barry, who travels to Brentford, while the rest of the squad is set up to exploit a favourable-looking fixture list.

Kinsky starts in goal at home to Ipswich, with the goalkeeper rotation working well despite the presence of Trafford in the wider squad. The defence is expected to feature Gabriel away to Newcastle, Silva at home to Nottingham Forest and D. Kyper away to Hull. The Newcastle trip is not ideal for Arsenal defenders, but the overall team strength means there is little pressure to make a defensive change.

The midfield five contains Kudus at home to Ipswich, Rogers and Palmer against Leeds, Groß, and Manzambi at home to Sunderland. Palmer and Haaland provide the premium core, while the Ipswich, Leeds and Sunderland fixtures give the supporting players clear attacking upside.

Leno, Gonzalo and Calafiori are on the bench, with Calafiori the notable omission because he has Newcastle away. There is some uncertainty over whether to change that decision, but the squad is viewed as strong enough to hold its shape. The fixture run is considered especially appealing for Gameweek 11, much like the team’s favourable setup around Gameweek 10, so there are no major complaints or urgent transfer issues.
key_points: Haaland is captained at home to Fulham in Gameweek 11.
Kinsky starts against Ipswich, with the goalkeeper rotation also benefiting from Trafford’s fixture schedule.
Gabriel is selected despite Arsenal travelling to Newcastle, while Calafiori is currently benched for the same fixture.
Palmer faces Leeds and Kudus hosts Ipswich, giving the midfield strong home-fixture appeal.
Manzambi’s home match against Sunderland is another key fixture in the five-man midfield.
The squad is being kept largely intact because the Gameweek 11 fixture run looks particularly strong.

items.title: MIDFIELDER SPECIAL 💥| FPL WATCHLIST GW11 WITH FPL HARRY 🔎| WIRTZ, MANZAMBI + MBEUMO | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Cole Palmer faces sale pressure as Aston Villa midfielders emerge for Gameweek 11
items.summary:
Cole Palmer is no longer an automatic hold despite Chelsea’s attractive home fixtures against Leeds, Crystal Palace and Liverpool. His lack of attacking output, combined with Chelsea’s dependence on the fitness of João Pedro, makes him the main midfield sale candidate. However, there is no standout direct replacement: with only one free transfer, the preference is to hold Palmer and retain flexibility, especially while João Pedro’s availability after the international break remains unclear. Palmer becomes much easier to sell if João Pedro is fit, as Chelsea’s attack then carries more appeal without needing Palmer’s premium price.

Aston Villa offer the best short-term midfield punt. Their next five fixtures are Sunderland at home, Ipswich away, Everton at home, Crystal Palace at home and Coventry away, giving them the strongest attacking schedule. Man Zambi is favoured for his more advanced role and explosive potential, although his minutes are not secure; John McGinn has penalties but is also being substituted regularly, while Alisson is the cheaper route at £4.9m. These are moves best made by managers with multiple free transfers, allowing a short-term Villa bet before reassessing the midfield.

Pascal Groß remains the safest established purchase for managers who do not own him: he has reliable minutes, penalties and a strong longer-term schedule, although he sits on four yellow cards. Marcus Tavernier is still preferred to Rayan despite the same suspension risk, because Bournemouth’s fixtures remain excellent through to around Gameweek 30 and Tavernier is more likely to produce steady returns. Bournemouth’s Krupi is not yet a convincing buy due to likely rotation with Kluivert and Evanilson, even if he is added to the European squad.

Liverpool’s run of Manchester United, Sunderland and Chelsea in three of the next four brings Florian Wirtz into consideration after his first league goal, but he remains a punt rather than a premium certainty. He starts regularly but has largely delivered modest assist-led returns, while Szoboszlai has uncertain penalty security and reduced minute security. Alexander Isak is the most attractive Liverpool attacker in isolation, but cheaper forwards such as Jackson, Barry, Evanilson and a fit João Pedro make it difficult to justify using one of three forward slots on him.

Longer term, Morgan Gibbs-White and Manchester United assets are the main alternatives to Palmer. Gibbs-White has penalties and stronger minutes, although Nottingham Forest’s immediate fixtures are less appealing. United’s attack is already functioning better than their defence, and a possible new manager could improve the appeal of Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo and Cunha after the Liverpool match, particularly for Coventry and Crystal Palace in Gameweeks 14 and 15. In defence, Van Hecke is a priority replacement for Lewis Hall ahead of Ipswich, with Schär an alternative for managers targeting Liverpool’s favourable festive fixtures.
key_points: Hold Cole Palmer with one free transfer unless João Pedro is confirmed fit or there is a clear plan for the money saved; sell consideration increases sharply if João Pedro is ruled out again.
Target Aston Villa midfielders for the next five matches, with Man Zambi the preferred attacking punt, McGinn offering penalties and Alisson the budget option.
Pascal Groß remains the leading dependable midfield buy thanks to penalties and secure minutes, but he is one booking from suspension.
Tavernier stays ahead of Rayan as Bournemouth’s most reliable midfield option despite being on four yellow cards; avoid Krupi until his league role is clearer.
Wirtz is Liverpool’s most interesting midfield punt for Gameweek 11 onwards, but his return profile and possible Christmas rotation make him less convincing than a true premium.
Gibbs-White and potential Manchester United assets, especially Bruno Fernandes or Mbeumo, are the favoured longer-term Palmer replacements after United face Liverpool.
Prioritise Lewis Hall to Van Hecke for Gameweek 11, while Schär is a viable differential for Liverpool’s Villa, Coventry, Hull, Sunderland and Palace run.
Haaland remains the clear captaincy choice at home to Fulham, while Barry’s recent chance volume makes him difficult to bench despite selection pressure elsewhere.

items.title: MY FIRST FPL GW11 TRANSFER PLANS! 🥶 PALMER HAS TO GO? #premierleague #fpl #football
items.headline: João Pedro fitness holds the key to Palmer decision ahead of Gameweek 11
items.summary:
The Gameweek 11 plan is to keep faith with a 4-4-2 and, ideally, roll the sole available free transfer. The squad is finally in a position the manager is comfortable with, with João Pedro currently on the bench and enough depth to avoid making a move unless fresh news creates a problem during the international break.

João Pedro is the main fitness watch. His availability and whether he returns to Chelsea training could affect not only his own place in the squad but also the prospects of Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers. If João Pedro is ruled out for a longer spell, he is no longer viewed as a desirable hold; Palmer could also become expendable after a run of underwhelming returns.

The difficulty is that replacing Palmer is not straightforward. Pascal Groß, Tair and Morgan Rogers are already owned, while the alternative midfield punts include Bryan Mbeumo, Morgan Gibbs-White, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Brighton options such as Jack Hinshelwood or Gomez. None is convincing enough to force an early move, particularly with Palmer still carrying upside.

Unless João Pedro news or another issue changes the picture before Gameweek 11, the priority is patience. Rolling the transfer would begin building a bank of two or three free transfers, giving greater flexibility to react to injuries, form swings and the possible Palmer decision in later weeks.
key_points: Set up in a 4-4-2 for Gameweek 11, with João Pedro currently benched.
Roll the one available free transfer unless international-break team news creates a clear problem.
Monitor João Pedro's fitness and Chelsea training status, as it could influence both his own value and the outlook for Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers.
Palmer remains a concern after disappointing returns, but finding a replacement midfielder is the main obstacle to selling.
Bryan Mbeumo, Morgan Gibbs-White, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Brighton midfielders are considered possible but unconvincing alternatives.
The longer-term aim is to accumulate two or three free transfers after reaching a more satisfactory squad structure.

items.title: MY FPL GW11 TRANSFER PLANS 📝 TIME TO SELL PALMER? 🥶 BUT TO WHO? | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Joao Pedro fitness dictates Harry’s Gameweek 11 transfer plan as Palmer becomes a growing concern
items.summary:
Harry enters Gameweek 11 with one free transfer and £0.5m in the bank, aiming to roll unless Joao Pedro remains unavailable and another starter becomes an issue. His current squad is led by David Raya, Calafiori, Van Hecke, Antonio Silva, De Cuyper, Pascal Gross, Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers, Tavernier, Nicolas Jackson and Erling Haaland, with Joao Pedro and Mkhitaryan providing bench cover. Haaland is the intended captain despite Manchester City’s recent form, with Jackson vice-captain.

The key decision is Joao Pedro’s recovery ahead of Chelsea’s home match against Leeds. Harry initially expects him back after the international break but is less certain following a guarded update from Xavi Alonso. If Pedro is fit, he is content to retain Chelsea’s attacking triple-up of Pedro, Rogers and Palmer for Leeds, Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace. If Pedro is out, the appeal of Palmer and the wider Chelsea attack falls sharply. Evanilson, Barry, Calvert-Lewin and potentially Isak are considered as forward alternatives, but none is compelling enough to force an early move unless Pedro’s absence is confirmed.

Palmer is the main medium-term sell candidate after another poor display. His underlying numbers are weak for his price: he ranks 22nd among midfielders for expected goal involvement per 90, has only three big chances all season and one is a penalty. Yet Harry does not see an obvious replacement and therefore prefers patience over a reactive downgrade. Morgan Rogers remains a long-term hold because of his price and the lack of convincing midfield alternatives, while Gross and Tavernier are also retained despite yellow-card risks.

Defensively, Harry is satisfied for now but flags De Cuyper and Calafiori as possible rotation concerns during the congested run of 10 gameweeks in 45 days. Vuskovic is the likely replacement if De Cuyper loses minutes, while Calafiori could become Gabriel, Konsa if his role is secure, or Vuskovic if Arsenal’s premium defensive double-up becomes too expensive. The priority is to bank transfers for rotation, injuries and suspensions, with Gross, Antonio Silva and Tavernier all one booking from a ban. Palmer could eventually make way for Mbeumo, Gibbs-White, Manzambi or Bruno Fernandes if Manchester United’s managerial situation improves and a clearer midfield target emerges.
key_points: Roll the Gameweek 11 transfer unless Joao Pedro is unavailable and another starting player also becomes a problem.
Captain Erling Haaland against the backdrop of recent Manchester City struggles, with Nicolas Jackson as vice-captain.
Joao Pedro’s fitness for Leeds at home is pivotal: his return supports retaining Palmer and Rogers, while another absence weakens the Chelsea triple-up.
Cole Palmer is a planned future sale rather than an urgent Gameweek 11 transfer, as his form and underlying numbers are poor but replacements are unconvincing.
Evanilson, Barry, Calvert-Lewin and Isak are possible Joao Pedro replacements if Chelsea confirm a longer absence.
Monitor De Cuyper and Calafiori for Christmas-period rotation; Vuskovic is the preferred value defensive replacement, with Gabriel or Konsa alternative Arsenal routes.
Gross, Antonio Silva and Tavernier sit on four yellow cards, making transfer flexibility especially valuable during the compressed November-December schedule.
Potential Palmer replacements later include Bryan Mbeumo, Morgan Gibbs-White, Manzambi and Bruno Fernandes, depending on fixtures, minutes and Manchester United’s next manager.

items.title: THE NEXT FPL TEMPLATE 📝 | THE FPL SCOUTCAST GAMEWEEK 11 🚨| FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Defenders and budget midfielders reshape the FPL template as Trafford and Rodoni emerge
items.summary:
Defence remains the strongest source of FPL value after 10 gameweeks, with reliable starters capable of banking defensive contributions (DefCon) preferred to expensive but inconsistent attackers. Arsenal’s David Raya, Gabriel, Jurrien Timber and Riccardo Calafiori remain attractive because of clean-sheet potential, while Tottenham’s Luka Vuskovic and Bournemouth’s Mihailo Murmurovic offer regular DefCon points at cheaper prices. Managers are urged to consider four or even five playable defenders rather than automatically loading funds into midfield and attack.

Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford is highlighted as a standout alternative to Raya. His save and bonus-point potential, plus home fixtures against Coventry in Gameweek 12, Ipswich in Gameweek 14 and Fulham in Gameweek 16, make him viable either as a set-and-forget pick or alongside Tottenham’s Anton Kinsky in a rotation. Suzuki is another low-owned goalkeeper to monitor, with Sunderland, Everton, Crystal Palace and Coventry among the favourable fixtures from Gameweek 11 onwards. Rotating keepers creates selection risk, however, so the preferred pairings are those with an obvious weekly fixture decision.

Timber is a low-owned Arsenal differential if he retains the first-choice right-back role, while Sunderland’s Nordi Mukiele and Liverpool’s Jeremie Frimpong are identified as potential defensive additions. Mukiele offers DefCon security and occasional attacking upside, while Liverpool’s fixtures improve from around Gameweek 15 and Frimpong provides a cheaper route into their back line than Virgil van Dijk. The key is to avoid ultra-cheap defensive enablers and instead build a group of five defenders who can be rotated according to fixtures, with one benchable option each week.

The midfield market is far less convincing. Cole Palmer’s price is increasingly difficult to justify given his subdued output over an extended period, even though penalties preserve his upside. A major downgrade from Palmer should not be made blindly, but cheaper midfielders can facilitate investment in defence. Aston Villa captain John McGinn is particularly appealing: he is on penalties while Emi Buendia is absent, Villa have an excellent short-term schedule and McGinn has produced two goals, four assists and a missed penalty across his last seven starts. Florian Wirtz, Dango Ouattara, Josh Rodon and Julio Enciso are lower-owned alternatives, with Rodon’s penalties, 0.48 expected goals per 90 and upcoming Palace, Leeds and Ipswich fixtures making him a useful rotation enabler.

There is little reason to gamble on differential forwards while the established options continue to dominate ownership and returns. Liam Delap has begun converting chances, Marmoush has Ipswich, Sunderland and Fulham in his next three fixtures, and Brian Brobbey has physical presence, but all carry major doubts over consistency, finishing or minutes. Barry is the more convincing lower-owned forward, sitting only just above the 10% ownership cut-off after strong underlying numbers and recent returns. For now, transfer priority should usually be on strengthening the defence rather than replacing premium strikers with speculative picks.
key_points: James Trafford is a leading goalkeeper differential, with saves, bonus potential and favourable Leeds home fixtures from Gameweek 12 onwards.
A Trafford-Kinsky rotation works on fixtures, but goalkeeper rotations add an avoidable weekly selection headache unless one choice is clearly superior.
Vuskovic, Murmurovic, Mukiele and Frimpong are attractive defensive options because DefCon points make dependable 90-minute defenders unusually valuable.
Jurrien Timber is a 1%-owned Arsenal differential if he keeps the right-back role, combining clean-sheet potential with more attacking upside than Arsenal’s centre-backs.
Managers should consider moving towards four or five playable defenders and spending less on cheap defensive enablers.
John McGinn is a midfield target for Villa’s favourable run, with penalties and strong recent returns strengthening his case.
Cole Palmer’s near-£10m price is under pressure after a long period of limited output, although his penalties mean selling him remains a calculated risk.
Avoid speculative moves for Delap, Marmoush or Brobbey unless their minutes and output improve; Barry is the more credible lower-owned forward option.

items.title: My Early Transfer Plans for Gameweek 11 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Haaland remains the clear captain as early Hall-to-Vuskovic move reshapes defence
items.summary:
Haaland is the straightforward captaincy choice, with Nicolas Jackson also locked in up front. The defensive core remains Raya and Calafiori, despite Arsenal’s trip to Newcastle, which is no longer viewed as the intimidating fixture it once was. Van Hecke is already in place for a favourable home match and has been in strong recent form.

The only transfer made is Lewis Hall to Vuskovic, completed early to beat a price rise. Making a move during the international break carries an obvious injury risk, but Vuskovic is a planned buy and combines well with Diop as a cheap defensive rotation. There is no immediate need to force further changes at the back, although Arsenal defensive cover may need reassessment in the coming weeks; an injury to either William Saliba or Gabriel could make a cheaper Arsenal replacement particularly attractive.

Mbeumo’s recent returns have been underwhelming, but he is worth holding for the fixture run from Gameweek 12 to Gameweek 15. He can be benched this week in favour of Calvert-Lewin or Konsa, while an alternative is to sell Sangare for a midfielder such as Tavernier or Kudus and start the replacement instead. Palmer and Rogers are also holds: Leeds at home is a reasonable fixture and both offer dependable minutes despite a recent lack of attacking output.

Pascal Gross stays in the squad after delivering consistently this season, with his yellow-card position not enough to justify a sale for an existing owner. The approach is therefore patient rather than aggressive: bank on the current premiums and strong-minute players, use the new budget-defender pairing for flexibility, and delay further defensive surgery until Gameweek 12 or 13 if needed.
key_points: Captain Haaland, with Nicolas Jackson retained as a non-negotiable forward option.
Lewis Hall is sold early for Vuskovic ahead of a price rise, despite the international-break injury risk.
Raya and Calafiori are retained for Arsenal’s trip to Newcastle, while Van Hecke remains a strong home-fixture starter.
Mbeumo is held for his Gameweek 12-15 fixture run and can be benched this week for Calvert-Lewin or Konsa.
A midfield switch from Sangare to Tavernier or Kudus is an alternative route to field a stronger XI this week.
Palmer, Rogers and Pascal Gross are all retained because of minutes security, fixtures and existing value.
Arsenal’s defence is monitored for Gameweek 12 or 13 changes, especially if Saliba or Gabriel suffer an injury.

items.title: YOU SHOULD FREE HIT IN GAMEWEEK __
items.headline: Gameweek 16 emerges as the standout Free Hit option if Erling Haaland is sold
items.summary:
There is no single must-play Free Hit week between Gameweeks 11 and 16, because many managers already own the obvious players with strong fixtures. The best approach is often to manage normally, retain flexibility and use the chip when a short-term problem emerges: one-week injuries, suspensions, a surprise Haaland absence or several key assets missing at once. Tavernier, Silva and Groß are all one booking from suspension, which could create exactly that sort of opportunity. If no clear opening appears, Gameweek 19 is the final fallback before the first set of chips expires.

Gameweek 11 is not especially attractive for an unplanned Free Hit, with Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Aston Villa, Brighton and Spurs all enjoying decent fixtures and likely to be well represented in existing squads. Gameweek 12 has a stronger structural case because Manchester City face Arsenal, allowing managers heavily invested in both sides to temporarily move away from that fixture. A draft includes Leeds and Brighton defensive doubles, Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo, plus Alexander Isak, Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Nicolas Jackson; however, it only truly pays off for squads carrying multiple City and Arsenal players.

Gameweeks 13 to 15 are more team-dependent. Gameweek 13 offers Liverpool at home to Sunderland, Manchester City against Leeds and Chelsea versus Crystal Palace, but it is a midweek round and carries rotation risk. Gameweek 14 is appealing for managers short of Bournemouth, Leeds and Manchester United assets: Bournemouth host Hull, Leeds host Ipswich and United host Coventry. Fernandes is a high-upside differential captaincy option against Coventry, even with Haaland facing Brentford. Gameweek 15 instead suits managers overloaded on Bournemouth and Chelsea players, who face Arsenal and Manchester City respectively, while Liverpool host Leeds and Arsenal defenders remain viable against Bournemouth.

Gameweek 16 looks strongest on paper, particularly for anyone selling Haaland beforehand. City host Hull, Bournemouth host Coventry and Brighton host Ipswich, creating scope for aggressive triples from all three clubs alongside Arsenal defenders and Isak against Spurs. The City selection can be informed by the preceding Carabao Cup tie against Bradford, with a rested player such as Rayan Cherki, Phil Foden, Jérémy Doku or a defender becoming a sharp punt. Managers keeping Haaland should first establish their preferred Free Hit week; if Gameweek 16 is not needed, it can instead be an excellent Triple Captain opportunity for him.

If managers choose to wait, Gameweek 19 provides a reliable deadline-day escape route. Liverpool host Coventry and Arsenal host Ipswich, making triples from both sides attractive, while Haaland hosts Spurs. A sample side centres on Arsenal defenders David Raya, Riccardo Calafiori and Gabriel, Liverpool trio Isak, Florian Wirtz and Virgil van Dijk, plus Brighton assets against Manchester United. All first-half chips must be used by Gameweek 19, as a new allocation arrives from Gameweek 20.
key_points: Do not force a Free Hit for Gameweek 11 unless your squad is poorly set up, as many popular teams already have favourable fixtures.
Gameweek 12 is most useful for managers holding several Arsenal and Manchester City players who want to avoid their head-to-head match.
Gameweek 14 offers a differential captaincy route with Bruno Fernandes at home to Coventry, while Bournemouth host Hull and Leeds host Ipswich.
Gameweek 15 is more appealing for squads carrying multiple Bournemouth and Chelsea assets, with Bournemouth away to Arsenal and Chelsea away to Manchester City.
Gameweek 16 is the leading Free Hit candidate for managers who sell Haaland, as City host Hull, Bournemouth host Coventry and Brighton host Ipswich.
Use the Carabao Cup team news before Gameweek 16 to identify rested Manchester City attackers or defenders likely to start against Hull.
Keep the chip flexible for one-week injuries, suspensions or late leaks, especially if Tavernier, Silva and Groß collect bans.
Gameweek 19 is the final chance to use the first Free Hit and is a strong fallback because Liverpool host Coventry and Arsenal host Ipswich.

items.title: GW10 Is Over... Here's What I'm Doing in GW11!
items.headline: Vuskovic emerges as the Gameweek 11 defensive priority as midfielders lose FPL value
items.summary:
Gameweek 10 reinforces an unusual FPL trend: defenders and forwards dominate the value picks while midfield options increasingly rely on penalties. Nine defenders sit in the top 20 overall scorers, led by Brighton pair Diper and Vuskovic, while only three midfielders make that group — Gross, Tavernier and the rotation-prone Cherki. With premium midfielders such as Palmer, Saka, Salah and Bruno Fernandes either injured, out of form or playing in struggling attacks, a three-man midfield — or even two midfielders in favourable weeks — looks increasingly viable.

Chelsea are the main attacking concern. Their defeat to Sunderland follows several unconvincing attacking displays, with Palmer offering little open-play threat and recently relying on a penalty for returns. Managers doubled up on Chelsea attack should consider reducing exposure, especially if planning to Free Hit in Gameweek 13, when Chelsea host Crystal Palace. Manchester United and Aston Villa remain teams to target with attackers after their high-scoring meeting, but neither looks dependable for clean sheets. Mbeumo remains a hold despite blanking against Villa: he continues to play close to 90 minutes in a striker role and has good fixtures against Coventry and Crystal Palace in Gameweeks 14 and 15.

The immediate Gameweek 11 move is Konsa to Vuskovic. William Saliba's recovery creates a growing minutes risk for Konsa, even if Konsa is still likely to start against Newcastle. Vuskovic is viewed as close to certain to start against Hull, carries greater attacking and defensive-contribution potential, and Brighton have a marginally better clean-sheet probability than Arsenal this week. The transfer is partly proactive and partly a move to beat likely price changes, but it also fits the longer-term plan because Brighton's fixture run is excellent apart from Bournemouth away in Gameweek 13.

The preferred Gameweek 11 setup starts Gross and likely retains Palmer and Rogers despite limited enthusiasm for either, while Mbeumo can be benched against Liverpool. Schade becomes a possible alternative starter because Thiago's three-match suspension makes him Brentford's likely penalty taker against Everton and Manchester United. Looking ahead, Palmer to Manzambi in Gameweek 12 could fund Barry to Calvert-Lewin for Coventry at home, although Barry's improving form makes that far from certain. A Gameweek 13 Free Hit remains the intended chip plan, allowing a short-term Chelsea attacking triple-up against Crystal Palace before returning to a squad built around Brighton assets, strong defenders and in-form forwards.
key_points: Prioritise Vuskovic for Gameweek 11, with Konsa the planned sale because Saliba's return threatens his security of minutes.
Brighton host Hull in Gameweek 11 and Vuskovic offers a slightly better clean-sheet outlook than Arsenal's Konsa against Newcastle, plus stronger attacking upside.
Chelsea attackers, particularly Palmer, are under review after another poor attacking display against Sunderland; a Gameweek 13 Free Hit can restore Chelsea coverage for Crystal Palace.
Mbeumo remains a hold despite the Liverpool fixture, as his striker role, minutes and Gameweeks 14-15 fixtures against Coventry and Crystal Palace retain appeal.
Schade is a potential Gameweek 11 starter over Palmer or Rogers, with Thiago suspended for three matches and Schade expected to inherit Brentford penalties.
The lack of reliable premium and defensive-contribution midfielders favours three-at-the-back midfield selections and heavier investment in defenders and forwards.
A possible Gameweek 12 route is Palmer to Manzambi and Barry to Calvert-Lewin, targeting Calvert-Lewin's home match against Coventry, but Barry's form makes the move optional.
Gameweek 13 remains the planned Free Hit window, chiefly to navigate Brighton's Bournemouth away fixture and target Chelsea's home game against Crystal Palace.

items.title: 15 things we've learned ahead of Gameweek 11 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Thiago suspension and Vardy-Gray knocks force Gameweek 11 transfer decisions
items.summary:
Thiago is an immediate sell after his red card brings a three-match suspension, while Jamie Vardy and Gray are also priority exits after both leave at half-time with knocks. João Pedro owners should wait for Javi Alonso’s expected Gameweek 11 update rather than making an early move, particularly if they have already held him through recent uncertainty.

Yellow-card risk is mounting for Tavernier, Silver and Pascal Groß, who are all one booking from a one-match ban. Groß faces Hull next, which may encourage managers to hold for one more week, but the disciplinary situation should factor into transfer planning. Konsa looks likely to start in Gameweek 11 but carries greater medium-term selection risk, while Saliba’s Under-21s minutes suggest he is nearing a return to Arsenal’s starting side.

De Bruyne and Vicario lead the defensive scoring charts and remain strong options, while Tino Livramento has six goals in 10 gameweeks at under £6m. Livramento’s output has been exceptional, but his favourable fixture run has largely passed, so buying now carries more schedule risk than buying earlier. Van Hecke offers a steadier route: he has returned at least four points in seven of the last eight gameweeks, and the fixtures improve after Liverpool away despite three recent blanks.

In attack, Palmer and Rogers have each managed only one goal and no assists across the last four gameweeks, tempering expectations. Verts is a quieter alternative after starting every match and delivering one goal plus three assists in the past four rounds. McGinn also strengthens his appeal at £5.4m after scoring from the penalty spot despite a recent miss. Gibbs-White’s latest attacking return makes him a reasonable hold, but Cherki is not yet a buy despite scoring on his start: his minutes remain uncertain and Arsenal away in Gameweek 12 is an awkward immediate fixture.
key_points: Sell Thiago after his red card results in a three-game suspension.
Move on Vardy and Gray after both suffer half-time knocks.
Wait for Gameweek 11 news on João Pedro before transferring him out.
Tavernier, Silver and Pascal Groß are each one yellow card away from a one-match ban.
Livramento has six goals in 10 gameweeks but faces a tougher fixture spell after an excellent run.
Van Hecke remains a viable hold, with favourable fixtures following Liverpool away and seven four-point-plus scores in his last eight gameweeks.
Avoid rushing for Cherki despite his goal, as his minutes are uncertain and Arsenal away follows in Gameweek 12.
McGinn at £5.4m and Verts, with one goal and three assists in four gameweeks, offer improving midfield value.

items.title: BEST PLAYERS SO FAR! 🚀 | FPL GENERAL'S GAMEWEEK 11 TRANSFER PLANS ✅ | FPL Tips 2026/27
items.headline: Isak joins Haaland and Jackson as FPL’s preferred front three ahead of Gameweek 11
items.summary:
The emerging FPL template favours a stronger defence and forward line, with midfield increasingly treated as a source of value rather than a place to spend heavily. The recommended Gameweek 11 setup is often 4-4-2, using cheap, reliable midfield options and premium defensive contributors. Haaland is still the leading captain for Manchester City’s home match against Fulham, despite concerns over City’s form and Pep Guardiola’s uncertain midfield selections.

Liverpool’s improving attack and favourable run to Gameweek 20 make Alexander Isak a standout forward target. He has seven goals, consistently collects bonus when he scores and provides a credible captaincy alternative in weeks when Haaland is less appealing. The preferred three-man frontline is Haaland, Isak and Nicolas Jackson, with Jackson retained for Chelsea’s immediate fixtures despite the team’s reliance on the injured João Pedro. João Pedro is viewed as a strong future switch around Gameweek 17, when Chelsea’s fixtures worsen and his own run against Coventry, Ipswich, Newcastle and Crystal Palace improves.

At the back, Brighton’s De Cuyper is described as close to essential after his exceptional attacking output, clean sheets and sustained role. The leading additions are centre-backs who can bank defensive-contribution points: Brighton’s Vuskovic and Leeds’ Mahrovic are particularly attractive, while Tottenham’s Van Hecke combines defensive-contribution potential with a major set-piece threat. Bournemouth’s Antonio Silva is another value option, although his four yellow cards create a suspension risk. Arsenal assets remain valuable, with Raya secure in goal and Gabriel offering both clean-sheet potential and the flexibility of an expensive defender who can be downgraded later to fund moves elsewhere.

The immediate transfer plan is to sell Manchester City defender Gvardiol for Vuskovic or Van Hecke, bench Dominic Calvert-Lewin away at Chelsea and play four defenders. Calvert-Lewin remains a sell candidate after limited returns, especially away from home, while Arsenal’s Calafiori and Conceição carry minutes concerns. Morgan Gibbs-White is frustrating but not an urgent sale: Nottingham Forest’s fixtures are favourable and their performance against Manchester City offers hope that their attack is beginning to convert underlying numbers.

Midfield alternatives are plentiful and cheap. Gross remains a high-value Brighton pick despite sitting on four yellow cards, while Rodoni is highlighted as an outstanding £4.9m enabling midfielder because he starts regularly, takes penalties and combines 17 shots with 17 chances created. Tavernier is preferred to more expensive Aston Villa midfielders, while Rogers is favoured over Cole Palmer as the Chelsea asset to keep. Palmer, Bruno Fernandes and Manchester City midfielders are viewed as expendable because of inconsistent form, uncertain minutes or inflated prices.
key_points: Captain Haaland for Gameweek 11 at home to Fulham, but Isak is a serious alternative captaincy option over Liverpool’s strong fixture run.
Prioritise a Gvardiol exit for Vuskovic or Van Hecke and use a 4-4-2, with Calvert-Lewin benched away to Chelsea.
De Cuyper is the premium defensive priority, while Vuskovic, Mahrovic, Van Hecke and Antonio Silva offer strong defensive-contribution value.
Keep Raya and consider Gabriel as Arsenal’s premium defensive option; Calafiori and Conceição have greater minutes risk.
Isak, Haaland and Jackson are the preferred forward trio, with João Pedro a likely Jackson replacement around Gameweek 17.
Rodoni is a standout £4.9m midfield enabler due to penalties, secure minutes and strong attacking numbers.
Retain Gibbs-White for now if transfers are needed elsewhere, as Nottingham Forest’s fixtures improve and their attack may be turning a corner.
Sell or avoid expensive midfield uncertainty: Palmer is less attractive than Rogers, while Bruno Fernandes and Manchester City midfielders lack reliability.

items.title: I've made a transfer! ✅ FPL GW11 Early Thoughts 🔥
items.headline: Haaland remains the Gameweek 11 captain despite a tempting Gameweek 12 exit plan
items.summary:
Erling Haaland remains the preferred captain for Gameweek 11 at home to Fulham, and selling him is not recommended in most cases despite two blanks and Arsenal away in Gameweek 12. His upcoming captaincy appeal quickly returns, notably against Leeds in Gameweek 13 and Hull in Gameweek 16, while Brentford away and Chelsea at home are also serviceable fixtures. A Haaland sale to fund Isak and Bruno Fernandes is a viable high-risk differential, particularly for managers holding a Free Hit, but it depends heavily on Bruno delivering and Isak staying fit through a busy winter schedule. Free Hitting in a week when Bruno or Isak has a standout fixture is viewed as the safer way to access them without dismantling a Haaland structure.

Bournemouth pair Tavernier and Silva are both one yellow card from a one-match suspension, with the threshold still set at five bookings until 19 matches have been played. Existing owners should hold and simply use their bench when a ban arrives. Tavernier remains worth considering as a new signing because he is among the best midfield options at his price, but buyers need sufficient bench cover and should avoid accumulating several players near suspension at once. Silva is less compelling because alternatives such as Vuskovic, Van Hecke, Hill and Murillo offer comparable defensive value without the immediate booking risk.

Pascal Gross is also on four yellows but is still endorsed at £6.3m or below: he plays heavy minutes, takes penalties and set pieces, and has a favourable six-game schedule led by Hull at home, Everton at home and Ipswich at home. Cole Palmer and Rogers are frustrating after just one goal and no assists apiece over the last four gameweeks, but neither requires an urgent sale. Rogers has respectable underlying numbers and acceptable fixtures, while Palmer's output and underlying data are concerning for £9.8m but his secure minutes, penalties and Leeds at home in Gameweek 11 make holding preferable unless a manager has a clear replacement such as Bruno Fernandes.

Among defenders, Vuskovic narrowly beats Van Hecke as the longer-term purchase because Brighton's next six fixtures are stronger and he can be played regularly. Van Hecke is still an excellent option, especially for Ipswich at home in Gameweek 11 or for rotation with Murillo. The squad discussed has already moved early from Lewis Hall to Vuskovic, securing him before a price rise; the move is justified by confidence that Vuskovic is the preferred target and by having three free transfers plus £1.8m in reserve. With Haaland captained, Gross starting and Bournemouth's Mbeumo retained despite Liverpool away, the likely plan is to bank another transfer rather than force a move for Tavernier, Kudus or a fifth defender.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Fulham in Gameweek 11; his Gameweek 13 Leeds home fixture makes a Gameweek 12 sale difficult to justify.
A Haaland-to-Isak route with Bruno Fernandes funded in midfield is a viable differential for Gameweek 12, but is best attempted with a Free Hit available for Gameweek 16.
Tavernier and Silva are on four yellow cards, so current owners should hold but new buyers must plan for a likely one-match ban.
Tavernier remains an acceptable risk because of his value and attacking appeal, while Silva is less attractive than Vuskovic, Van Hecke, Hill or Murillo.
Buy Gross despite his four-yellow-card risk if bench cover is available, given his penalties, set pieces, minutes and favourable upcoming fixtures.
Hold Rogers and generally hold Palmer for Gameweek 11; neither has an obvious must-buy replacement, though Palmer to Bruno Fernandes is under consideration.
Prefer Vuskovic over Van Hecke for the next six gameweeks, although Van Hecke is marginally appealing immediately for Ipswich at home.
Lewis Hall is sold early for Vuskovic, while Konza is retained temporarily because he could regain value if Arsenal's defensive options suffer setbacks.

items.title: FPL GW11 TRANSFER PLANS ✅ MY GAMEWEEK 11 TEAM 🎯
items.headline: Vuskovic move leads Gameweek 11 plans as Joao Pedro’s fitness decides Jackson transfer
items.summary:
Gameweek 11 planning centres on Brighton defender Vuskovic, with a move from Arsenal’s Concer the preferred transfer. Concer has performed well while William Saliba is absent, but Saliba is building match fitness and could soon reclaim his place. Vuskovic offers a similarly strong clean-sheet chance against Hull, has penalty-winning and bonus potential, and Brighton’s defensive form makes him one of the standout budget defenders. The intention is to make that switch, bank the second free transfer and potentially reach three free transfers by Gameweek 13 ahead of a planned Free Hit in Gameweek 14.

Joao Pedro versus Jackson is the main forward dilemma. Jackson has Sunderland at home in Gameweek 11 and looks attractive after his return against Aston Villa, while Chelsea’s attack has underwhelmed in recent weeks despite their good fixtures. However, Joao Pedro has Leeds at home, is a differential and could match or outscore Jackson if fit after the international break. The Jackson move is therefore favoured only if Pedro remains unavailable, or if the funds released materially improve another part of the squad; otherwise, spending a transfer to sell Pedro and potentially needing another to buy him back is seen as an unnecessary risk.

Erling Haaland remains a hold for Fulham at home, but his tougher Gameweek 12-15 run — Arsenal, Leeds, Brentford and Chelsea — makes a future sale worth considering. Moving off Haaland could fund a stronger spread of assets such as Joao Pedro, Bruno Fernandes and Gabriel, and offers a potential differential route for managers chasing rank. For now, the safer call is to retain him, particularly with a home fixture immediately ahead.

The starting Gameweek 11 side is Raya; Saliba, Diper, Van Heck and Concer; Palmer, Rogers and Gross; Barry, Haaland and Joao Pedro, with Mbeumo, Sharda and Mendy on the bench. Barry remains viable despite Everton’s less appealing next fixtures because his 7.8 expected goal involvement is almost level with Haaland’s 7.9, he has secure minutes and could become even more valuable if confirmed as Everton’s penalty taker. Longer-term defensive targets include Gabriel, Virgil van Dijk and Vuskovic, while Morgan Gibbs-White is a midfield option from Gameweek 13 due to strong underlying numbers and a favourable fixture run.

A Gameweek 14 Free Hit is under consideration to exploit Hull at Bournemouth, Ipswich at Leeds and Coventry at Manchester United. The aggressive draft stacks Bournemouth defenders against Hull and Manchester United midfielders against Coventry, accepting the one-week nature of the gamble. That chip plan affects current transfers: there is little value in buying players solely for the Gameweek 14 fixtures if they will be replaced by the Free Hit squad.
key_points: Prioritise Concer to Vuskovic in Gameweek 11, then roll the remaining free transfer if no major international-break news changes the plan.
Keep Joao Pedro if he returns to fitness; move to Jackson primarily if Pedro remains out, rather than chasing Chelsea’s Sunderland home fixture.
Hold Haaland for Fulham at home, but reassess from Gameweek 12 when Arsenal, Leeds, Brentford and Chelsea make a premium redistribution viable.
Barry’s elite 7.8 xGI, reliable minutes and possible penalty duties keep him appealing despite Everton’s mixed upcoming schedule.
Avoid buying Leeds assets for Chelsea away in Gameweek 11, but consider them from Gameweek 12 for fixtures including Coventry, Ipswich and Fulham at home.
Target Arsenal, Liverpool, Spurs, Brighton and Bournemouth defenders; Gabriel and Van Dijk are premium long-term options, while Vuskovic is the standout cheaper pick.
Plan around a possible Gameweek 14 Free Hit, with Bournemouth versus Hull and Manchester United versus Coventry the key fixtures to attack.
Sell Brentford’s Thiago after his red card rules him out of Everton, Manchester United and Arsenal fixtures.

items.title: FPL Kneejerk Gameweek 11 🔥 Barry Haul ✅ BIG Red Arrow 😬
items.headline: Vuskovic tops Gameweek 11 defensive shortlist as FPL managers weigh five-at-the-back
items.summary:
A red arrow to around 110,000 after 59 points does not prompt major attacking surgery. Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Bryan Mbeumo all frustrate, but the midfield market lacks convincing replacements: Marcus Tavernier and Antoine Semenyo carry four-yellow-card suspension risks, while options such as Morgan Gibbs-White, Florian Wirtz, Jérémy Doku and John McGinn are viewed more as punts or enablers than clear upgrades. Palmer’s home fixture against Leeds in Gameweek 11 also makes an immediate move to Bruno Fernandes unattractive.

Fernandes is nevertheless a credible Palmer replacement from Gameweek 12 through 15, particularly for captaincy, but it is a short-term switch that likely requires another transfer to reverse. Erling Haaland remains the preferred Gameweek 11 captain at home to Fulham despite two consecutive blanks, with Alexander Isak, Palmer and Nicolas Jackson in the wider conversation. Selling Haaland for Fernandes is only tempting for managers without a Free Hit; Haaland appears the better captain in more of the upcoming weeks, while a Gameweek 14 Free Hit can target Fernandes instead.

The immediate priority is defence. Luka Vuskovic is the leading transfer target thanks to a strong fixture run and his value, with Lewis Hall and Jurrien Timber alternatives depending on budget and existing squad structure. Hall has little appeal beyond Ipswich in Gameweek 15, while Arsenal’s Ben White/William Saliba fitness situation makes Jakub Kiwior’s minutes less secure. Vuskovic is preferred long term to Van Hecke by a narrow margin, although Van Hecke has the better Gameweek 11 fixture and both are viable alongside attacking defender De Cuyper.

Five defenders is increasingly viable, particularly for teams with strong budget defenders and uncertainty in midfield. Joe Rodon or John McGinn can function as cheap enablers, with McGinn attractive if he retains penalties, but neither is compelling enough to force out Palmer, Rogers or Mbeumo. Mbeumo is held through a difficult Liverpool fixture because Brentford’s Gameweeks 12-15 schedule improves sharply. Pascal Groß is also retained as a strong penalty-taking midfield option, though his four yellow cards create the same suspension concern as Tavernier and Bournemouth’s Marcos Senesi.

Illia Zabarnyi and Murillo remain strong defensive assets but are not priorities before difficult fixtures; Murillo is more appealing in Gameweek 12 or 16, especially for managers Free Hitting in Gameweek 14. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is held for his favourable run including Ipswich, Coventry and Hull, rather than being sold reactively for Barry after the latter’s returns in a soft fixture spell. Barry remains an excellent cheap forward to own, but Brentford, Liverpool, Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest make this a less attractive time for non-owners to buy.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Fulham at home in Gameweek 11; Isak, Palmer and Jackson are secondary options.
Vuskovic is the preferred defensive transfer, but wait through the international break unless protecting a price rise is worth the injury risk.
Avoid forcing out Palmer, Rogers or Mbeumo, as the current midfield alternatives are not clear long-term upgrades.
Consider Palmer to Bruno Fernandes from Gameweek 12, but the move is more appealing without a Gameweek 14 Free Hit and may need reversing later.
Mbeumo is worth holding through Liverpool because Brentford’s fixtures improve from Gameweek 12 to 15.
Tavernier, Groß and Senesi are each on four yellow cards, one booking away from a Premier League suspension.
Murillo is best targeted in Gameweek 12 or Gameweek 16 if a Gameweek 14 Free Hit removes one of his best fixtures.
Hold Calvert-Lewin for his upcoming fixtures and penalties; Barry is a strong enabler but is not an urgent buy after his favourable recent opponents.

items.title: 44 POINTS SO FAR 🔥 | FPL CHAI'S GW11 TRANSFER PLANS | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Gabriel captaincy pays off as Gameweek 11 sets up Haaland, Kudus and a Free Hit 14 plan
items.summary:
Gabriel proves the standout captaincy call in Gameweek 10, combining Arsenal’s near-guaranteed clean-sheet potential with defensive contribution points. Haaland remains a reasonable captain after coming close to returning, but Arsenal’s defensive reliability makes Gabriel, Saliba and Calafiori viable alternatives when the champions have favourable fixtures. Arsenal are expected to become even harder to score against when William Saliba returns, while Newcastle’s blunt attack makes their Gameweek 11 trip to the Emirates another appealing defensive target.

The Gameweek 11 squad is in strong shape without an immediate transfer need. Haaland is set to captain against Fulham at home, while Kudus has Ipswich at home despite an underwhelming Tottenham performance in the previous round. Palmer and Rogers also have Leeds at home, Pascal Gross faces Hull away and Barry travels to Brentford. Barry’s 16-point return reinforces his value at under £6m: his finishing can be erratic, but his movement, aerial ability and consistent big-chance volume make him a strong hold, even through a tougher Everton run. He is not necessarily a priority buy before Brentford, Liverpool, Aston Villa, Fulham and Brighton, but he remains playable or benchable at his price.

There is little reason to force differentials while the current template is delivering. The core of Haaland, Palmer, Rogers, Gross, Arsenal defenders and budget defensive-contribution options is strong, and straightforward moves such as Lewis Hall to Bournemouth’s Silva are favoured over speculative punts. Cody Gakpo is identified as one of the better midfield differentials because of Liverpool’s favourable run against Crystal Palace, Manchester United, Everton, Sunderland, Leeds, Tottenham and Hull. Rayan is another lower-owned attacking option, while Jude Bellingham is considered a form-based punt despite not yet matching last season’s FPL output. Manchester United assets, particularly Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo and Cunha, could re-emerge if the international break brings a managerial lift.

Bench Boost strategy is also shaped by avoiding unnecessary future planning constraints. Playing it in Gameweek 10 is defensible even without a huge immediate score, as it removes the need to preserve a deep bench and avoids complications from Gross being one yellow card from a suspension. Looking further ahead, Gameweek 14 is the preferred Free Hit target: Arsenal face Tottenham, creating a clash for managers with heavy coverage of both sides; Bournemouth host Hull, offering an opportunity to load up on their attackers; Chelsea meet Liverpool; and Manchester United host Coventry. A Free Hit could also target Leeds against Ipswich, with options such as Mbeumo, Fernandes, Cunha, Calvert-Lewin, Rayan and Illan Meslier potentially replacing seven or more regular starters.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 11 against Fulham at home, but Arsenal defenders remain legitimate captaincy alternatives when the fixture is right.
Keep Barry after his 16-point haul: he is a value hold because he continues to get high-quality chances, though he is not an essential buy before Everton’s tougher run.
Kudus remains a hold for Tottenham’s home match against Ipswich, with his 82-minute outing and fixture outweighing one poor team performance.
Consider starting Calafiori over Silva in Gameweek 11, as Arsenal’s clean-sheet odds against Newcastle appear stronger than Silva’s fixture against improving Nottingham Forest.

Gameweek 14 is a leading Free Hit option because it allows managers to avoid Arsenal versus Tottenham assets while attacking Bournemouth versus Hull, Manchester United versus Coventry and Leeds versus Ipswich.
Cody Gakpo is the preferred midfield differential thanks to Liverpool’s strong upcoming fixture run; Rayan and Jude Bellingham are alternative lower-owned punts.
A Bench Boost in Gameweek 10 is justified as a way to remove future squad-planning restrictions, with Gross’s proximity to a yellow-card ban adding urgency.
Raya and Trafford are increasingly attractive goalkeeper targets, although buying Raya can require sacrificing the funds needed for Gabriel alongside Haaland and Palmer.

items.title: FPL GW10 LIVE DEADLINE STREAM 📸  -4 HIT CONFIRMED FOR 2 TRANSFERS 💥 | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Haaland keeps the armband as Bournemouth double-up drives Gameweek 10 plan
items.summary:
Erling Haaland remains the preferred captain for Gameweek 10 despite Nottingham Forest’s strong home defensive record. Arsenal defenders Gabriel and Riccardo Calafiori have excellent clean-sheet and attacking-return projections against Hull and are viable alternative captains, while Alexander Isak is the standout differential armband choice against a Crystal Palace side in poor defensive form. However, there is reluctance to captain a defender after previous disappointments, so Haaland remains the pragmatic pick; this is not a week to triple-captain him.

The squad takes a minus-four to sell Morgan Gibbs-White and Bobby Thomas for Bournemouth pair Marcus Tavernier and Antonio Silva. The move is primarily long-term: Bournemouth’s schedule remains attractive through to the next Wildcard window, and the early transfers capture price rises while avoiding being left behind by Gibbs-White’s potential further drops. The hit also creates a deeper bench for Gameweek 11 if Joao Pedro or Pascal Gross remain unavailable, although benching Spurs defender Van de Ven/Van Hecke-type coverage after a recent haul is acknowledged as uncomfortable.

Joao Pedro is still started purely to trigger an automatic substitution, with Antonio Silva first in line from the bench. Pedro is not expected to feature after Brighton give no meaningful update before the international break. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is a doubt but is still considered likely to start; managers who own both him and a Spurs defender can start Calvert-Lewin and use the defender as cover if he misses out. Pascal Gross is playable but no longer untouchable, with his output reduced alongside Hinshlewood; managers with strong alternatives such as Marcus Tavernier, Bryan Mbeumo or a good defender can reasonably bench him.

David Raya is the priority goalkeeper buy, even for a hit in some cases, because Arsenal’s defensive ownership is so high and Raya can be started almost every week. Gabriel is the premium defensive target if funds are available, but the £3m gap to cheaper options such as Brighton’s Diego Coppola/Vuskovic, Spurs defenders and Antonio Silva matters when midfield premiums become attractive again. Lewis Hall, Ait-Nouri and expensive Manchester City defenders such as Josko Gvardiol are sell candidates, while Evanilson is the preferred forward purchase ahead of Nicolas Jackson and Barry after looking far more central and dangerous for Bournemouth.
key_points: Captain Haaland by default; Isak is the preferred differential captain, while Gabriel and Calafiori are strong but riskier defensive alternatives.
The confirmed minus-four is Gibbs-White to Tavernier and Bobby Thomas to Antonio Silva, targeting Bournemouth’s long fixture run and price rises.
Start Joao Pedro only for the auto-substitution, as he is unlikely to play before the international break; Antonio Silva is the intended replacement.
Buy David Raya if possible, including for a hit when replacing a weak goalkeeper such as Horn or Sánchez, and then play him regularly.

Gabriel is the best Arsenal defender on a Wildcard, but cheaper defenders such as Vuskovic, Dier/Kadioglu-type Brighton options, Van de Ven/Van Hecke and Antonio Silva offer better squad-value balance.
Evanilson is now the leading forward transfer target, with Jackson also attractive; Calvert-Lewin owners can consider upgrading if they lack reliable bench cover.
Bench Boost is viable in Gameweek 10 or 11 only if the bench is genuinely strong; avoid forcing it with uncertain players such as Bobby Thomas or injured doubts.
Avoid buying Declan Rice, Gakpo, Cherki or Gvardiol purely on short-term appeal, due to limited explosiveness, rotation risk or difficult upcoming fixtures.
